extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator / literate public interested in poetry, manners, and politics (early 18th-century)
extracted.subtask_description: Critical guidance and examples for reading and judging epic poetry (Milton's Paradise Lost) alongside prescriptive remarks on manners, marriage, and the satiric training of statesmen. Emphasises poetic devices, similes, characterization, and structural choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain, simple, and unadorned opening lines
rubrics_metrics.description: These Lines are perhaps as plain, simple and unadorned as any of the whole Poem, in which Particular the Author has conformed himself to the Example of Homer and the Precept of Horace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An epic's exordium should be clear and unpretending; simplicity in opening lines (invocation and statement of subject) aligns with classical exemplars and is a virtue rather than a defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invocation suited to the poem's subject
rubrics_metrics.description: His Invocation to a Work which turns in a great measure upon the Creation of the World, is very properly made to the Muse who inspired Moses ... and to the Holy Spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an invocation or address appropriate to the subject-matter and source tradition (e.g., invoking the Muse/Holy Spirit for creation themes) so the opening coheres with the poem's origins and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural and happy transition to the fable
rubrics_metrics.description: This whole Exordium rises very happily into noble Language and Sentiment, as I think the Transition to the Fable is exquisitely beautiful and natural.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move from exposition to the narrative (fable) smoothly; the shift should feel inevitable and elevate into the primary story without awkwardness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of noble, finely imagined circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nine Days Astonishment, in which the Angels lay entranced after their dreadful Overthrow and Fall from Heaven ... is a noble Circumstance, and very finely imagined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include striking, well-conceived incidents that enhance grandeur and wonder; such 'noble circumstances' should deepen the poem's emotional and imaginative impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fruitful and imaginative worldbuilding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Hell into Seas of Fire, and into firm Ground impregnated with the same furious Element, with that particular Circumstance of the Exclusion of Hope from those Infernal Regions, are Instances of the same great and fruitful Invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventive, internally coherent cosmologies and distinctive features (e.g., geography, laws like 'Exclusion of Hope') enrich epic scope and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization via first speeches that interweave passions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Thoughts in the first Speech and Description of Satan ... are wonderfully proper to give us a full Idea of him. His Pride, Envy and Revenge, Obstinacy, Despair and Impenitence, are all of them very artfully interwoven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce major characters with speeches that compound their dominant passions and traits; a single introductory speech can encapsulate a complex character by interweaving motifs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid and terrifying physical imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole part of this great Enemy of Mankind is filled with such Incidents as are very apt to raise and terrifie the Readers Imagination ... his being the first that awakens out of the general Trance, with his Posture on the burning Lake, his rising from it, and the Description of his Shield and Spear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, theatrical physical details (posture, weapons, movement) to produce awe and terror; vivid sensory description strengthens dramatic presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powerful auditory and performative imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: He call'd so loud, that all the hollow deep Of Hell resounded--
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ sound and performative cues (calls, shouts, cries) to convey scale and effect; auditory imagery can amplify the grandeur of scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passages worked to sublime climax
rubrics_metrics.description: But there is no single Passage in the whole Poem worked up to a greater Sublimity, than that wherein his Person is described in those celebrated Lines: --He, above the rest In shape and gesture proudly eminent Stood like a Tower, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build selected passages toward sublimity through heightened diction, rhythm, and carefully staged imagery; certain moments should reach an elevated, memorable pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of sentiments with character and nature
rubrics_metrics.description: His Sentiments are every way answerable to his Character, and suitable to a created Being of the most exalted and most depraved Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that what characters say and feel coheres with their established nature and the metaphysical logic of the poem; sentiments must match character to feel authentic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Villainy expressed as absurdity, not credible doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: Amidst those Impieties which this Enraged Spirit utters ... the Author has taken care to introduce none that is not big with absurdity, and incapable of shocking a Religious Reader ... bearing only a Semblance of Worth, not Substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray wicked or irreligious rhetoric as rhetorically plausible for the character but ultimately absurd or hollow, avoiding endorsement that would genuinely offend readers' values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of humanizing emotional moments (tears)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor must I here omit that beautiful Circumstance of his bursting out in Tears, upon his Survey of those innumerable Spirits whom he had involved in the same Guilt and Ruin with himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate moments of unexpected pathos (e.g., tears) even in depraved characters to complexify them and evoke sympathy or horror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learned catalogues and classical allusions enrich the poem
rubrics_metrics.description: The Catalogue of Evil Spirits has abundance of Learning in it, and a very agreeable turn of Poetry, which rises ... from describing the Places where they were worshipped, by those beautiful Marks of Rivers so frequent among the Ancient Poets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use erudition, mythic catalogues, and learned allusions (analogous to Homer or Virgil) to lend gravitas and cultural depth to epic narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character sketches should foreshadow speeches and behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: The Characters of Moloch and Belial prepare the Readers Mind for their respective Speeches and Behaviour in the second and sixth Book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shape early descriptions of characters so they naturally anticipate and justify their later actions and oratory; preparation increases coherence and dramatic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate tone for mythic/romantic episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Account of Thammuz is finely Romantick, and suitable to what we read among the Ancients of the Worship which was paid to that Idol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match tone and manner (romantic, elegiac, comic) to the mythic or cultural material so episodes feel authentic and resonant with their sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce explanatory mechanisms to make marvels plausible
rubrics_metrics.description: The Passage in the Catalogue, explaining the manner how Spirits transform themselves by Contractions or Enlargement of their Dimensions, is introduced with great Judgment, to make way for several surprizing Accidents in the Sequel of the Poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including marvelous transformations or miracles, provide internal rules/explanations early so later marvels feel plausible rather than arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain internal hierarchy/consistency among supernatural beings
rubrics_metrics.description: For he tells us, that notwithstanding the vulgar, among the fallen Spirits, contracted their Forms, those of the first Rank and Dignity still preserved their natural Dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve consistent differences (rank, scale, behavior) among supernatural entities to reinforce dramatic and mythic order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive settings and theatrical constructions (Pandæmonium, Mammon)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Character of Mammon and the Description of the Pandæmonium, are full of Beauties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create striking, original settings and personifications (palaces, standards, lights) that showcase poetic imagination and support the poem's mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended similes developed into great ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: When Milton alludes either to Things or Persons, he never quits his Simile till it rises to some very great Idea, which is often foreign to the Occasion that gave Birth to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow similes to extend and develop beyond the immediate likeness, turning a brief comparison into a broader, 'glorious Image' that enriches the poem's conceptual reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid trivial or quaint similes; prefer grand similitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ignorant Readers, who have formed their Taste upon the quaint Similes, and little Turns of Wit, which are so much in Vogue among Modern Poets, cannot relish these Beauties which are of a much higher Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eschew petty conceits and trivial cleverness in favor of large, elevated comparisons that suit epic scale; the critic privileges weighty, noble comparisons over witty niceties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparisons need only general resemblance; avoid over-precision
rubrics_metrics.description: That it is not necessary in Poetry for the Points of the Comparison to correspond with one another exactly, but that a general Resemblance is sufficient, and that too much Nicety in this Particular favours of the Rhetorician and Epigrammatist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit broad, suggestive correspondences in similes rather than literal or point-by-point matches; excessive exactness reduces poetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comparisons to amuse, relieve, and diversify
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons ... are not introduced only to illustrate and embellish the Discourse, but to amuse and relax the Mind of the Reader, by frequently disengaging him from too painful an Attention to the Principal Subject, and by leading him into other agreeable Images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy similes and comparisons as structural devices to give readers relief, variety, and supplementary imagery—short episodes that diversify the main fable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epic structural principle: fable, episodes, similes, metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: If we look into the Conduct of Homer, Virgil and Milton, as the great Fable is the Soul of each Poem, so to give their Works an agreeable Variety, their Episodes are so many short Fables, and their Similes so many short Episodes; to which you may add ... their Metaphors are so many short Similes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure long poems so the central fable is reinforced by episodic diversions and pictorial similes/metaphors; think of episodes/similes as embedded mini-fables that enrich variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to apparel preserves mutual regard in intimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Emilia's Observation teaches her, that as little Inadvertencies and Neglects cast a Blemish upon a great Character; so the Neglect of Apparel, even among the most intimate Friends, does insensibly lessen their Regards to each other, by creating a Familiarity too low and contemptible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small attentions to dress and appearance matter in close relationships: neglect of apparel reduces esteem and breeds contemptuous familiarity even among intimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic virtue: obstinacy of goodness and unprovoked submission
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Help of these, and a thousand other nameless Arts, which tis easier for her to practise than for another to express, by the Obstinacy of her Goodness and unprovoked Submission ... Bromius is become a Man of Sense and a kind Husband, and Emilia a happy Wife.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistent goodness and modest, patient behavior (described as 'unprovoked Submission') are presented as effective practical arts for preserving marriage and improving a husband's character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Love as motive for self-improvement and industry
rubrics_metrics.description: There is not a downright Enmity, but a great Coldness between our Parents ... I have for some Years indulged a Passion ... A certain Complacency to all the World, a strong Desire to oblige where-ever it lay in my Power, and a circumspect Behaviour ... have rendered me more particularly acceptable ... Love has had the same good Effect upon my Fortune; and I have encreased in Riches ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portrayal of love as a positive motivation: romantic attachment should inspire better manners, industry, and circumspection, which in turn improve social standing and fortune.

rubrics_metrics.name: State- or diplomacy-skills satire: 'state legerdemain' (espionage and forgery)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first is to instruct the Students in State Legerdemain, as how to take off the Impression of a Seal, to split a Wafer, to open a Letter, to fold it up again, with other the like ingenious Feats of Dexterity and Art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirically enumerates technical clandestine arts a political academy would teach; as a critical note: successful diplomacy (here caricatured) often relies on secretive technical skills—seal-forgery, letter-opening—though presented as morally dubious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posture-master: mastery of political grimace and gesture
rubrics_metrics.description: This Artist is to teach them how to nod judiciously, to shrug up their Shoulders in a dubious Case, to connive with either Eye, and in a Word, the whole Practice of Political Grimace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonverbal behaviour—gestures, shrugs, winks—are essential diplomatic craft (satirically): training in mannered carriage and expressive ambiguity is depicted as part of political education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language-master: the art of indirect and evasive diplomatic speech
rubrics_metrics.description: This is to instruct them in the Style proper for a Foreign Minister ... If one of them asks another, what a-clock it is, the other is to answer him indirectly, and, if possible, to turn off the Question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diplomatic style prefers circumspection and evasiveness; practitioners should be trained to answer indirectly, deflect, and employ ambiguity to avoid commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cipher and political characters: coded correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fourth Professor is to teach the whole Art of Political Characters and Hieroglyphics; ... they are not to send a Note to one another ... which is not written in Cypher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mastery of codes, ciphers, and symbolic notation for secure political communication is presented as a formal skill for statesmen (satirically emphasised).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jesuitical/diplomatic instruction: probable doctrines and finding loopholes
rubrics_metrics.description: Their Fifth Professor ... is to be well read in the Controversies of probable Doctrines, mental Reservation, and the Rights of Princes ... to teach them the Art of finding Flaws, Loop-holes, and Evasions, in the most solemn Compacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training in interpretive niceties, mental reservation, and techniques for exploiting textual ambiguity is shown as instrumental for diplomatic negotiation and legalistic evasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master of Ceremonies: mastery of courtly ceremony and postures
rubrics_metrics.description: This Gentleman is to give them Lectures upon those important Points of the Elbow Chair, and the Stair Head, to instruct them in the different Situations of the Right-Hand, and to furnish them with Bows and Inclinations of all Sizes, Measures and Proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fluency in ceremonial etiquette—bows, positions, gestures, and the subtleties of court manners—is critical for outward political performance and influence (satirically insisted upon).
